title: The restocker and its vehicles
summary: Stock does not simply appear in TCG Card Shop Simulator: the game runs deliveries through a restocker that arrives in a vehicle of its own, from a bike up to a helicopter.
body: Deliveries come through a restocker. The game keeps the restocking run as a system of its own, which is why an order arrives as a delivery rather than appearing on a shelf.

The vehicle is part of the order. The game sorts restockers into kinds, running from a bike through a van and a truck to a bigger truck and a helicopter, so the size of what you ordered is matched by how it turns up.
You can change how it is sorted. The game keeps sorting options for restocking, including by licence level and by cost in either direction, which is why the delivery list can be ordered to suit you.
The delivery has an icon of its own. The game uses its own restock-box icon, so a delivery is identifiable on screen rather than only in the world.
It ties to the licence level. Because sorting can be by licence level, what you are allowed to sell and what arrives are part of the same system.
What this entry does not tell you: what each vehicle costs, how much it carries, or how long a delivery takes. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Deliveries are run through a restocker rather than appearing directly.
Restockers come in kinds, running from a bike through vans and trucks to a helicopter.
facts.evidence: identifiers: Bike, Van, Truck, BigTruck, Helicopter

facts.claim: There is a set of sorting options for restocking, including by licence level and by cost.
The phone is what puts the shop into restock scanning mode.
The restocker's vans are named one by one, with two minivans among them.
